validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline does not touch Texas at all. Independently confirmed by FOUR sources, none derived from another: (1) Kinder Morgan's own company overview PDF (pipeline2.kindermorgan.com/Documents/SGP/SGP_CI_Cpny_Overview.pdf, retrieved same date as the sheet's LastUpdated 2023-08-23; verifier gives OK/200 liveness but its PDF-text extraction misses the content check on this doc -- confirmed by hand with pdftotext -layout, which reads: 'extends from Kinder Morgan, Inc.'s El Paso Natural Gas pipeline system, near Tucson, Arizona, to the United States-Mexico border near Sasabe, Arizona'); (2) EIA's own Today in Energy article (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=44856, verified OK/200 + content), an independent federal agency, describing 'the Sierrita export pipeline from Tucson, Arizona, to the U.S. border with Mexico'; (3) Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, verified OK/200 + content via the verifier's own sec.gov UA retry), which places the asset as 'Near Tucson, Arizona, to the U.S.-Mexico border near Sasabe, Arizona'; (4) Mexico's federal gas-pipeline status register (gob.mx PDF, verified OK/200 liveness, content confirmed by hand with pdftotext -- lists the Sierrita Gas Pipeline (Tucson-Sasabe) under Entidad = 'Arizona'). Existence, classification (interstate/international natural gas transmission lateral, not gathering), and ownership are all otherwise confirmed clean -- see the confirmed-caveat entry below. This is a single-field location defect, not an existence or duplicate concern.

validity.recommendation: Update Capacity from 200.00 MMcf/d to reflect the 2020 compression expansion -- current nameplate is materially higher. Kinder Morgan's own current company overview states 523,640 Dth/d; EIA independently confirms a +0.32 Bcf/d (320 MMcf/d) 'Sierrita Pima Expansion' completed in early 2020 on top of the original ~200 MMcf/d design capacity, which brackets the same ~520 MMcf/d total. Length (60 mi) and Diameter (36 in) are unaffected -- this was a compression/looping-style throughput increase, not new pipe, consistent with the same physical lateral described throughout.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current value of 200.00 MMcf/d is the pipeline's ORIGINAL 2014 design capacity, not its current one. That original figure is well corroborated for 2014: Natural Gas Intelligence's Oct 31 2014 in-service article ('The approximately $204 million pipeline has the capacity to deliver 200 MMcf/d of gas', verified OK/200 + content) and Mexico's gob.mx federal register ('Capacidad (mmpcd) 195*', verified OK/200 liveness, content confirmed by hand) both independently agree on ~195-200 MMcf/d as of 2014. But the pipeline was subsequently expanded: EIA's Today in Energy piece (Aug 24 2020, independent US federal source, verified OK/200 + content on 'Sierrita' + '0.32') states 'the 0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion, was also completed in early 2020, increasing the capacity on the Sierrita export pipeline from Tucson, Arizona, to the U.S. border with Mexico.' Kinder Morgan's own current company overview PDF (retrieved 2023-08-23, the same date as the sheet's own LastUpdated -- verifier OK/200 liveness, content hand-confirmed via pdftotext) independently states the pipeline 'currently provides 523,640 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of firm transportation capacity... The Sierrita pipeline system was built in 2014 and expanded in 2020.' 200 + 320 = 520 MMcf/d, which is in the same range as 523,640 Dth/d (Dth and Mcf are approximately but not exactly equivalent for pipeline gas, so I'm not proposing an exact converted figure as a drop-in replacement -- that conversion depends on the gas's actual heating content, which none of these sources state). Net: the sheet's Capacity is stale by roughly 2.5x. I did not add a Capacity [ref] fill pairing a source with the current (likely wrong) 200.00 value, since that would misrepresent a source that actually describes a higher current capacity as confirming the lower one -- this needs an Update-leg value change before a ref belongs on it.

validity.researcher_notes: Existence: extensively documented as a real, in-service pipeline -- SEC filings from BOTH joint-venture partners (Kinder Morgan's 2018 and 2022 Form 10-Ks, and Petroleos Mexicanos' own 2022 Form 20-F, all on SEC EDGAR and verified OK/200 with content confirmed), EIA, Mexico's federal gas-pipeline registry, Kinder Morgan's own investor-relations in-service press release (Oct 31 2014), Natural Gas Intelligence, and local press covering the pre-construction controversy (azcentral.com 2014, verified OK/200 + content). Not a phantom or GEM-only entity. Classification: correctly a natural-gas transmission lateral (36-inch, interstate + international), not a gathering/process line -- confirmed by every source above. No duplicate found against the 45-row TX-operating roster; Sierrita's Tucson-Sasabe/Sonora corridor is not shared with any other row in the set. Fuel = Gas: confirmed (all sources describe natural gas transportation; capacity stated in Dth/d and MMcf/d, gas-only units). StartYear1 = 2014: confirmed independently by Kinder Morgan's Oct 31 2014 in-service press release, the Oct 31 2014 Natural Gas Intelligence article, and Mexico's gob.mx register (fecha de operacion Dic/2014). Length = 60.00 mi: corroborated within normal rounding by NGI ('61-mile') and Mexico's register (97 km = 60.28 mi); Kinder Morgan's own 2018 and 2022 10-K asset tables both list the JV interest at exactly 60 miles. Diameter = 36.00 in: confirmed exactly by both NGI and Kinder Morgan's company overview ('36-inch diameter'). Owner1/2/3 (Kinder Morgan 35% / MGI Enterprises US LLC 35% / MIT Pipeline Investment Americas Inc 30%): confirmed at high tier by two genuinely independent parties to the JV itself -- Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K ('We operate Sierrita Gas Pipeline LLC and own a 35% interest... MGI Enterprises U.S. LLC, a subsidiary of PEMEX, owns 35%; and MIT Pipeline Investment Americas, Inc., a subsidiary of Mitsui & Co., Ltd, owns 30%') and Petroleos Mexicanos' own 2022 Form 20-F, which separately reports its 35.00% equity-method stake in 'Sierrita Gas Pipeline LLC' and notes the company 'was created on June 24, 2013' -- consistent with an in-service date the following year. SegmentCost = $200,000,000: a caveat, not a concern -- Natural Gas Intelligence reported an approximate $204 million project cost at construction (2014) and Mexico's federal register lists $182 million (MMUSD); the sheet's $200M sits between the two. A ~10% spread across two independent estimates for pipeline capex is ordinary reporting variance (budget vs. final, or differing cost scope), not a material conflict. Harvested-citation coverage: of the 17 citations on this row's wiki page, I opened and evaluated 14 (both Kinder Morgan 10-Ks, the Pemex 20-F, both Kinder Morgan investor documents, the Mexican federal register, EIA's Today in Energy piece and its general Natural Gas Data page, NGI, azcentral, and the Arizona Daily Independent/Fronteras background pieces on the pre-construction routing dispute). I did not open: IJGlobal's two project-database links (paywalled asset-transaction database, not needed given the SEC-filing-level corroboration already in hand), the Mitsui press release (now a dead 404 on mitsui.com -- confirmed by direct fetch, page reads 'The page you are looking for cannot be found'; not cited, not needed), and the Akron Beacon Journal general 2013 background piece on US-Mexico gas exports (not pipeline-specific).
